# Line and Edge Detection

Also called: Line Illustration, Edge Highlighting, Silhouette Detection

## Overview
Line and Edge Detection is a family of Non-Photorealistic Rendering (NPR) techniques designed to detect and render lines within volume data to communicate structure, shape, and boundaries [G]. It solves the problem of visualizing complex geometry and internal structures in volumetric datasets where traditional photorealistic rendering may obscure topological details [G]. What sets this family apart from its siblings is its specific focus on line-based abstraction rather than surface shading or contour outlines; it distinguishes itself from [Face-based volume rendering with edge highlights](2453-face-based-volume-rendering-with-edge-highlights.md) by generating lines that represent intrinsic surface properties (like curvature) rather than just silhouette edges, and from [Outline and Contour Generation](4137-outline-and-contour-generation.md) by often utilizing vector-oriented or texture-based approaches that are viewpoint-independent or analytically derived, rather than purely image-space depth-difference extraction [G].

## Subtopics

### [Line Illustration Detection](772-line-illustration-detection.md)
Focuses on line-based abstraction rather than surface shading or contour outlines. Distinguishes itself from [Face-based volume rendering with edge highlights](2453-face-based-volume-rendering-with-edge-highlights.md) by generating lines representing intrinsic surface properties, and from [Outline and Contour Generation](4137-outline-and-contour-generation.md) by utilizing vector-oriented or texture-based approaches. Choose when explicit analytical forms or viewpoint-independent line generation are required.

### [Face-based volume rendering with edge highlights](2453-face-based-volume-rendering-with-edge-highlights.md)
Renders volumetric data by coloring scalar cells while highlighting topological edges (faces of quads) for structural clarity. Distinguishes itself by operating on face-based primitives rather than skeletal lines, and integrates edge highlights directly into the volume fragment shader using a Per-Pixel Linked List (PPLL) for depth sorting. Choose when sharp edge highlights and alpha blending of semi-transparent cells are needed in a single pass.

### [Outline and Contour Generation](4137-outline-and-contour-generation.md)
Generates view-dependent lines to demarcate object boundaries and emphasize form. Distinguishes itself by unifying analytical and pixel-based paradigms, ranging from particle-based gradient analysis to curvature-thresholded fragment shaders. Choose when view-dependent silhouette extraction is preferred.

### [LOG-based Silhouette Detection](6322-log-based-silhouette-detection.md)
Identifies silhouette voxels for rendering sketch-like curves by replacing an exhaustive 3x3x3 subspace search with a precomputed Laplacian of Gaussian (LOG) value. Distinguishes itself by prioritizing performance while maintaining visual results. Choose when real-time silhouette detection is required.

### Voxel Highlight Edge Detection
Highlights cell boundaries based on distance to entry points during ray traversal [S1, unofficial]. Calculate entry point $hp = org + dir \times t_{cur}$ [S1, unofficial]. Calculate local cell coordinates $local = (hp - bmin) / cell$ [S1, unofficial]. Extract 2D face coordinates $f$ based on entry axis: if axis=0, $f=fract(local.yz)$; if axis=1, $f=fract(local.xz)$; if axis=2, $f=fract(local.xy)$ [S1, unofficial]. Calculate edge distance $edge = \min(\min(f.x, 1.0-f.x), \min(f.y, 1.0-f.y))$ [S1, unofficial]. If $edge < 0.06$, highlight color is yellow $(1.0, 0.85, 0.1)$; otherwise mix lit color with yellow at 0.35 weight [S1, unofficial].

### Hough Space Silhouette Detection
An approach by Li et al. to detect silhouettes in Hough space for edge sampling [S2]. Used in Li's edge sampling approach [S2].

### Object Space Enhancement
A pre-computed shape enhancement cue based on object-space analysis using a sharpened filter (Laplacian-like) on a 3x3x3 unit volume to enhance edges and contours, solving the concave/convex inconsistency of local illumination [S3, unofficial]. Select a 3x3x3 point unit volume surrounding the sampling center in the data volume [S3, unofficial]. Calculate the sharpened filter value $52f = [f(x+1, y, z) + f(x-1, y, z) + \dots + f(x+1, y+1, z+1)] - 26f(x, y, z)$, where $f(x,y,z)$ is the intensity of the sampling point [S3, unofficial]. Calculate the enhanced intensity $g(x,y,z) = f(x, y, z) - 52f$ [S3, unofficial]. Calculate the shape factor $S_{object} = g(x, y, z) + c$, where $c$ is a parameter to adjust the effect of object space enhancement [S3, unofficial]. Clamp the shape factor: if $g(x, y, z) + c > 1$, set it to 1 [S3, unofficial]. Local illumination alone cannot solve the display of concave parts; this cue makes up for that shortcoming [S3, unofficial]. The cue is pre-computed before ray casting, so it does not occupy rendering time, allowing real-time interactivity [S3, unofficial].
